intro_band.agent_remit_summary: The uAgents Framework Runtime is Fetch.ai's Python plumbing for autonomous agents that hold a cryptographic identity and blockchain wallet, register on the Almanac contract, and exchange typed messages over authenticated channels. The framework's duty is to hand every deployed agent a trustworthy foundation: a protected identity, cryptographically authenticated and replay-resistant inter-agent messaging, schema-validated inputs, and bounded, observable operation. Its authorized channels are the signed agent HTTP endpoint (`/submit`), the optional Agentverse mailbox/proxy, and the Fetch.ai Almanac/ledger; local inspector and administrative endpoints (`/messages`, `/connect`, `/disconnect`, `/agent_info`) are restricted to the local operator. It must never write private keys to disk in plaintext, expose administrative interfaces to unauthenticated remote callers, act on an unverified sender identity, or re-process a replayed or expired signed envelope.
intro_band.agent_structure_summary: A pure-Python framework (`uagents` 0.25.3 plus the `uagents-core` package), model-agnostic with no LLM or vector store on its own path. The inbound path is a hand-rolled ASGI app in `src/uagents/asgi.py` served by uvicorn: it validates envelopes against the pydantic `Envelope` schema, verifies ECDSA signatures via `envelope.verify()` for agent senders, and dispatches typed messages through `dispatch.py` to developer handlers registered on the `Agent` class in `agent.py`. The server hardcodes `HOST = "0.0.0.0"` and sets `forwarded_allow_ips="*"` and wildcard CORS; the agent inspector (which registers the `/agent_info`, `/messages`, `/connect`, `/disconnect` REST endpoints) is enabled by default. Identity and wallet keys are derived deterministically from a seed, but the name-based path in `storage/__init__.py` writes them to `private_keys.json` in cleartext, and no envelope replay/expiry validation exists anywhere on the receive path.

behavior_summary: The framework ships genuine cryptographic primitives — deterministic seed-derived identities and enforced ECDSA envelope-signature verification before dispatch — but its default network posture and secret handling undercut them. The dominant pattern is unauthenticated remote exposure by default: `HOST="0.0.0.0"` with the debug inspector enabled, `/agent_info` exempted from the loopback guard, and `forwarded_allow_ips="*"` letting a remote caller spoof `X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1` to reach the `/messages`, `/connect`, and `/disconnect` admin endpoints — the exact spoofed-loopback attack the remit names as bad behavior. Two independent trust gaps compound it: identity and wallet keys are persisted in cleartext `private_keys.json`, and signed envelopes carry `expires`/`nonce` fields that nothing on the receive path ever validates, so any captured envelope can be replayed to re-run a handler.

rules.rule_text: Executing operating-system shell commands or arbitrary code on behalf of a remote message sender.
Writing agent private keys, wallet keys, or seed phrases to disk in plaintext form.
Exposing administrative, introspection, or message-history interfaces to unauthenticated remote callers.
Acting on the claimed identity of a message sender without cryptographic proof of that identity.
Local agent inspector / admin endpoints (`/messages`, `/connect`, `/disconnect`, `/agent_info`) Restricted Yes — local operator only Must not be reachable by unauthenticated remote callers
Sensitive configuration secrets MUST NOT be embedded as literals in framework or agent source.
Binding the agent's HTTP server to a non-loopback (public) network interface.
Enabling remote reachability of the inspector / administrative endpoints.
Dispatching an inbound message from a non-user agent sender whose envelope signature has not been verified.
Accepting and re-processing a previously delivered (replayed) or expired signed envelope as if it were fresh.
Treating an unauthenticated, sender-asserted identity as trusted for any security decision.
Maximum retries before escalation: bounded; registration and delivery retries must be finite.
An inbound signed envelope fails signature verification.
Restarts must not change a seeded agent's identity or wallet address.

findings.summary: Administrative, introspection, and message-history endpoints are reachable by unauthenticated remote callers via a spoofable loopback guard on a default-public server.
findings.description: The agent inspector is enabled by default and registers the `/agent_info`, `/messages`, `/connect`, and `/disconnect` REST endpoints; the server binds `0.0.0.0`. The only guard on the reserved admin endpoints checks `scope["client"]` for `127.0.0.1`, yet the server sets `forwarded_allow_ips="*"`, so uvicorn overwrites the client address from an attacker-supplied `X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1` header — and `/agent_info` is exempt from the guard entirely. A remote caller can read cached message history and drive connect/disconnect, the exact spoofed-loopback bad behavior the remit names.
policy_rule_text: Exposing administrative, introspection, or message-history interfaces to unauthenticated remote callers.
Local agent inspector / admin endpoints (`/messages`, `/connect`, `/disconnect`, `/agent_info`) Restricted Yes — local operator only Must not be reachable by unauthenticated remote callers
Enabling remote reachability of the inspector / administrative endpoints.
Treating an unauthenticated, sender-asserted identity as trusted for any security decision.

evidence.snippet: reserved-endpoint guard `request_path in set(RESERVED_ENDPOINTS) - {"/agent_info"} and "127.0.0.1" not in scope["client"]` — /agent_info exempt, and client is spoofable because forwarded_allow_ips="*" at :184
enable_agent_inspector default True (:305) registers /agent_info, /messages, /connect, /disconnect handlers exposing agent info and cached message history

recommended_actions: Set `forwarded_allow_ips` to the explicit trusted proxy address(es) only (never `"*"`) in `ASGIServer.serve()`, and remove `/agent_info` from the loopback-guard exemption so every reserved endpoint enforces the local-caller check.
Default `enable_agent_inspector` to False and require explicit operator opt-in, and default the bind host to `127.0.0.1`.

findings.summary: Agent identity and wallet private keys are written to disk in cleartext JSON when an agent is created by name without a seed.
findings.description: `get_or_create_private_keys` calls `save_private_keys`, which serializes the identity private key and wallet private key as plaintext into `private_keys.json` in the process working directory with no encryption, keychain, or secret-manager indirection. These keys control the agent's on-chain identity and wallet assets, so a single filesystem read compromises both. This directly violates the remit's non-goal and forbidden-data-movement clauses against writing keys to disk in plaintext.
policy_rule_text: Writing agent private keys, wallet keys, or seed phrases to disk in plaintext form.

evidence.snippet: save_private_keys writes {"identity_key":..., "wallet_key":...} via json.dump to private_keys.json in cwd, no encryption (lines 113-127)
get_or_create_private_keys generates Identity/wallet keys and persists them in cleartext for the name-based (seedless) agent path

recommended_actions: Stop persisting raw private keys; derive them at runtime from an operator seed held in an environment variable or secret manager, or encrypt the key file at rest with an operator-supplied passphrase.
If a key cache is retained, restrict it to `0600` permissions and document it as a sensitive artifact that must be excluded from backups and version control.

findings.summary: Signed envelopes are never checked for replay or expiry, so a captured envelope can be re-submitted to re-run a handler.
findings.description: The `Envelope` schema carries `expires` and `nonce` fields that are folded into the signed digest, but the receive path only verifies the signature — it never rejects an envelope whose `expires` has passed and never tracks nonces or session/digest pairs to detect a replay. `expires` is read solely to size a sync-response timeout, and `dispatch_msg` performs no deduplication. Any party who captures a valid signed envelope can replay it verbatim and the target handler will execute again, the exact replay bad behavior the remit forbids.
policy_rule_text: Accepting and re-processing a previously delivered (replayed) or expired signed envelope as if it were fresh.

evidence.snippet: only `env.verify()` (signature) is checked before dispatch_msg; expires/nonce never validated — env.expires is read only at :390 to compute a timeout
dispatch_msg forwards to handlers with no nonce/session dedup or replay cache

recommended_actions: On the receive path in `asgi.py`, reject any envelope whose `expires` timestamp is in the past before dispatch, and require `expires` on signed agent envelopes.
Track a bounded set of recently-seen `(sender, session, nonce)` tuples (or digests) and drop duplicates, so a replayed signed envelope is discarded rather than re-dispatched.

findings.summary: The agent HTTP server binds to all interfaces by default with no loopback default and no operator approval step.
findings.description: `HOST` is hardcoded to `0.0.0.0` in `asgi.py`, so every agent exposes its `/submit` and inspector endpoints on all network interfaces from first run. The remit requires human approval before binding to a non-loopback interface, but there is no opt-in gate, no loopback default, and no warning — the public exposure is the unconditional default. This is the entry condition that makes the spoofed-loopback admin-access chain (PRAX-2026-07-27-001) remotely reachable.
policy_rule_text: Binding the agent's HTTP server to a non-loopback (public) network interface.

evidence.snippet: module-level `HOST = "0.0.0.0"` used unconditionally in uvicorn.Config(host=HOST, ...) at :179-181
serve() passes HOST directly with no configurable/loopback-default host and no approval check

recommended_actions: Default the bind host to `127.0.0.1` and expose the host as an explicit constructor/config argument, requiring the operator to opt in to a public bind.
Emit an operator-visible warning when a non-loopback host is configured, matching the remit's "alert operator" escalation for public binds.

findings.summary: A signature-verification failure is only logged as a warning and the envelope rejected; the remit's halt-and-alert escalation is not implemented.
findings.description: The remit classifies a failed envelope-signature verification as a halt-agent-and-alert-operator event. In code the failure path logs a warning and returns a 400 for that one request, with no operator alert, no structured security event, and no halt. Rejecting the single envelope is the correct data-plane action, but the absence of any alerting or durable security-event record means repeated forged-envelope attempts pass undetected.
policy_rule_text: An inbound signed envelope fails signature verification.

evidence.snippet: except branch logs `self._logger.warning(f"Failed to verify envelope: {err}")` and returns 400 — no operator alert, no structured security event, no halt

recommended_actions: Emit a structured, distinctly-typed security event on verification failure (sender, target, session) routed to the operator's alerting channel, separate from free-form warning logs.
Add a per-sender failed-verification counter with an operator-configurable alert threshold rather than silently rejecting each attempt.

findings.summary: The agent HTTP server returns a wildcard CORS policy allowing any web origin to drive requests to the agent.
findings.description: The server sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` for GET/POST/OPTIONS on every response. With credentials disabled the read-response risk is limited, but a malicious web page loaded in an operator's browser can still issue cross-origin POSTs to a locally-bound agent's `/submit` (including unsigned user-address messages), giving drive-by injection of agent input. Combined with the default public bind this widens the reachable request surface.

evidence.snippet: uvicorn headers hardcode ("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*") with Methods "GET, POST, OPTIONS" for all responses (lines 186-190)

recommended_actions: Replace the wildcard `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` with an operator-configurable allowlist of trusted origins, defaulting to none for the agent message endpoint.

findings.summary: Runtime dependencies are declared with floor-only version ranges, one entirely unbounded, weakening the declared supply-chain surface despite a committed lockfile.
findings.description: `pyproject.toml` pins every runtime dependency with a `>=` floor rather than an exact or bounded range, and `cosmpy (>=0.12.1)` has no upper bound at all. A committed `uv.lock` mitigates this for installs that honor the lock, but any consumer resolving from the manifest alone (or an unlocked install) is exposed to version-swap and dependency-confusion risk on a core cryptographic/ledger dependency.

evidence.snippet: dependencies use floor-only ranges; `cosmpy (>=0.12.1)` has no upper bound (lines 14-20)

recommended_actions: Add upper bounds to the runtime dependency ranges (especially `cosmpy`) and document the lockfile as the required install path for reproducible, provenance-checked builds.

findings.summary: Any caller can self-assert a `user`-prefixed sender address to skip signature verification, and unsigned handlers then receive an unauthenticated, spoofable sender.
findings.description: Signature verification is skipped whenever `is_user_address(env.sender)` is true, and that check is a pure string-prefix test on the self-declared sender field with no cryptographic proof behind it. Agent-to-agent messages are still verified, but any remote caller can present a `user...` address to reach unsigned/`allow_unverified` handlers with a fully attacker-chosen sender identity. A developer handler that makes a trust or routing decision on `sender` is therefore acting on an unauthenticated identity.
policy_rule_text: Acting on the claimed identity of a message sender without cryptographic proof of that identity.

evidence.snippet: `if not is_user_address(env.sender): env.verify()` — user-prefixed senders bypass verification; is_user_address is a prefix check on the self-asserted address
unsigned-handler path routes user-address messages to handlers with the unverified sender (lines 1455-1469)

recommended_actions: Document that `sender` on the unsigned/user path is unauthenticated and provide a framework helper that prevents trust or authorization decisions on an unverified sender.
Consider requiring a lightweight proof (per-session challenge) for user senders before routing to handlers that take security-relevant actions.

positives.title: Envelope signature verification enforced before dispatch
positives.description: Every inbound envelope from a non-user (agent) sender is ECDSA-verified against the claimed sender address before it is routed to any handler, and a verification failure rejects the message.

positives.title: Deterministic, restart-stable seed-derived identity
positives.description: Identity and wallet keys are derived deterministically from an operator seed, so a seeded agent keeps the same on-chain identity and wallet address across restarts.

positives.title: Schema-validated inbound message dispatch
positives.description: Inbound payloads are validated against declared pydantic message schemas before reaching a handler, giving a consistent input-validation boundary on the data plane.

positives.title: Committed dependency lockfile
positives.description: A full uv.lock is committed alongside pyproject.toml, giving reproducible dependency resolution despite the floor-only version ranges in the manifest.

positives.title: Private security disclosure policy
positives.description: SECURITY.md defines a private vulnerability-reporting channel and coordinated-disclosure process for the framework.

rows.content_type: plaintext JSON key-value store; optional inbound message history
rows.purpose: persists agent key-value state and, when store_message_history is enabled, inbound envelope history

raise_posture.weighted_rationale: Ad hoc. The framework has real, operative foundations — every inbound agent envelope is signature-verified before dispatch and every payload is pydantic-schema-validated — which keeps it off the floor, but the controls that would make it trustworthy at runtime are missing or defeated. Zero Trust is dragged down by a default public bind, a spoofable loopback admin guard, plaintext key persistence, and total absence of replay protection; adversarial testing and structured security monitoring are effectively absent. It is a capable messaging substrate whose secure operation depends heavily on the deploying developer overriding insecure defaults.

categories.name: Limit Your Domain
categories.rationale: Message dispatch is structurally constrained to registered pydantic schema digests — unrecognized schemas are logged and dropped (agent.py `_process_single_message`) — but the HTTP surface is bound to all interfaces by default and the reserved-endpoint set is only softly guarded, so the reachable surface exceeds the intended local-operator scope.

categories.name: Balance Your Knowledge Base
categories.rationale: Inbound payloads are consistently validated against declared pydantic message schemas before reaching any handler (asgi.py `Envelope.model_validate`, agent.py `model_class.parse_raw`), a real and uniformly applied input-validation control; there is no LLM context or RAG store on the framework's own path to poison.

categories.name: Implement Zero Trust
categories.rationale: Agent-sender envelope signatures are verified before dispatch (asgi.py:363-371) — a genuine operative control — but that is undercut by a default `0.0.0.0` bind, a `forwarded_allow_ips="*"` loopback guard that is trivially spoofable, plaintext private-key persistence, a self-assertable `user`-address verification bypass, and no replay/expiry validation at all.

categories.name: Manage Your Supply Chain
categories.rationale: A full `uv.lock` is committed and the framework version is pinned, giving reproducible resolution, but `pyproject.toml` declares runtime dependencies with floor-only `>=` ranges — `cosmpy (>=0.12.1)` has no upper bound — leaving the declared range open to version-swap risk if the lockfile is bypassed.

categories.name: Build an AI Red Team
categories.rationale: A functional unit-test suite exists (`tests/test_msg_verify.py`, `tests/test_server.py`) covering the signature happy path and REST routing, but there is no adversarial testing of replay, spoofed-loopback, or forwarded-IP bypass and no evidence that security testing drove any architectural change.

categories.name: Monitor Continuously
categories.rationale: The framework wires Python logging throughout and logs a warning on signature-verification failure, but logging is free-form console output with no structured security-event schema; the durable message-history record is off by default (`store_message_history=False`), leaving no action-level audit trail at runtime.
